Telegram._UserTenantMappings_doc: architecture.md §7.1 lines 1043-1062 is the canonical source for this section. Each KEY is a Telegram user ID (string form of the numeric id Telegram assigns) -- the same value the operator's user id MUST also be listed under Telegram:AllowedUserIds for Tier-1 onboarding to succeed. Each VALUE is a JSON ARRAY of workspace-binding objects (even single-workspace operators use a one-element array). The /start handler iterates the array and calls IOperatorRegistry.RegisterAsync once per entry, creating one OperatorBinding per workspace. Replace the example below with your real operator->workspace map before deploying; the placeholder user ids '000000000' / '111111111' are intentionally not in AllowedUserIds, so they cannot accidentally onboard.

OutboundQueue._Mode_doc: Stage 6.3 IOutboundQueue selection switch. 'Persistent' (default; this file) uses the EF-backed PersistentOutboundQueue (durable outbox with WAL fsync per message) suitable for Production. 'InMemory' (appsettings.Development.json) selects the bounded Channel<OutboundMessage>-backed dev queue so a developer's laptop never accumulates a stale messaging.db full of in-flight rows. When the key is absent, Program.cs falls back to environment-based selection: Development => InMemory, every other env => Persistent.
